name: IN-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about 21 points
Carson's incumbency and $1.1M raised versus a challenger with no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at 97-98%
No public polling; outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The Indianapolis-based district's D+21 lean, Carson's long incumbency, and his large financial edge over a little-known Republican challenger all point to an easy hold, and markets on Kalshi and Polymarket confirm near-certain Democratic odds.
model.watch: Only a dramatic national wave against Democrats or a major polling failure across similar districts could narrow the margin, though the outcome itself is very unlikely to be in doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
André Carson enters the general election as a heavy favorite in this Indianapolis-based district, which leans Democratic by roughly twenty points. He has raised more than $1.1 million and holds about $600,000 on hand, while Republican Patrick McAuley shows no reported fundraising. A Libertarian, James Sceniak, also appears on the ballot. Betting markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both put Carson's chances near ninety-seven to ninety-eight percent.

No public general-election polling covers the race, so the outlook rests on the district's strong Democratic lean, Carson's established incumbency, and the stark funding gap. Carson has won recent contests by wide margins, and nothing in the available evidence suggests a competitive dynamic is developing. The seat is rated Safe Democratic, with residual uncertainty driven more by turnout than by the identity of the winner.
